stories.title: Russia using North Korean missiles to strike Ukraine, Zelensky says
stories.summary: Ukraine's president says strikes in Zaporizhzhia - which killed at least six and injured 19 - involved ballistic missiles from Russia's ally.
stories.post: 📰 NEWS: Russia using North Korean missiles to strike Ukraine, Zelensky says. Ukraine's president says strikes in Zaporizhzhia - which killed at least six and injured 19 - involved ballistic missiles from Russia's ally. Source: BBC World.
article_sentences: Ukraine and Russia have continued striking each other overnight, with Volodymyr Zelensky accusing Moscow of using North Korean missiles.
The Ukrainian president said strikes in Zaporizhzhia - which killed at least six and injured at least 19 - involved ballistic missiles from Russia's ally.
In Voronezh, in southern Russia, warehouses belonging to the online retailer, Wildberries, were hit by Ukraine.
The company, known as Russia's Amazon, has been repeatedly targeted in recent weeks.

The attacks come a day after at least 13 people were killed, including one child, in Ukrainian drone strikes on the Russian republic of Tatarstan, more than 1,100 km (680 miles) from the Ukrainian border.
In a video address on Monday evening, Zelensky said "for the first time" Russia "cannot wage war without reinforcements from North Korea".

"The more North Korean strikes there are here in Ukraine, in Europe, the more their missiles and soldiers are used, the more they correct their shortcomings and blind spots", Zelensky said, adding that this poses a danger to the rest of the world.
In his address, Zelensky also hailed a successful air strike on a Russian petrochemical plant in western Siberia on Monday as a "very significant achievement" by the Ukrainian military.
He promised "more Ukrainian deep strikes, which should demonstrate to Russia and the Russians that peace is necessary".
It is not the first time Zelensky has accused Russia of receiving military assistance from North Korea.
He warned over the weekend that as many as 50,000 North Korean soldiers are being sent to join the military campaign defending Russian territory.
One person was injured in strikes on Kyiv, where air raid sirens sounded twice during the night.

stories.title: Colombia quake: Frantic search for survivors as over 2,700 reported missing
stories.summary: Magnitude 7.4 earthquake kills at least 132 people and causes widespread damage in western Colombia.
stories.post: 📰 NEWS: Colombia quake: Frantic search for survivors as over 2,700 reported missing. Magnitude 7.4 earthquake kills at least 132 people and causes widespread damage in western Colombia. Source: Al Jazeera.
article_sentences: Magnitude 7.4 earthquake kills at least 132 people and causes widespread damage in western Colombia.

Rescuers are searching through collapsed buildings in western Colombia for survivors after the country’s strongest earthquake this century killed at least 132 people and caused widespread devastation, according to local media.

Emergency teams in the worst affected cities, including Cali and Pereira, have been working through the night and into Tuesday, listening for signs of life and trying to reach people trapped beneath concrete and debris during the magnitude 7.4 earthquake.
The Choco region west of Cali and Pereira has also been impacted, but the extent of the damage is still not clear.
Authorities have warned that the death toll from Monday’s quake could rise as search teams reach more affected areas in a big challenge for newly elected far-right President Abelardo de la Espriella.
What is the death toll and extent of the damage?
Dozens of people were killed in Cali, located 280km (175 miles) southwest of the capital, Bogota.
On Monday President De la Espriella said 35 people were killed in the city.
Dozens of buildings were left leaning precariously or destroyed outright, forcing residents into the streets in the city of about 2.2 million people.
Local authorities farther north in the Risaralda region, where Pereira is located, said the death toll included at least 40 people killed there.
Authorities also confirmed nine people killed in the Choco region, two in the Caldas region and a 73-year-old in the Antioquia region.
At least 87 people were initially reported injured, but de la Espriella later reported 700 injured in Valle del Cauca alone.

stories.summary: Study finds technology could boost recoverable oil and gas reserves by 5% and cut cost of deepwater projects by 10% AI-driven productivity gains enable more planet-heating pollution from fossil fuels than they avoid from renewables, a study has found. Researchers modelled the technical potential for AI to boost clean power generation along with projections for how it can help produce coal, oil and gas. stories.title: Spain prepares for rare total solar eclipse as 2026 sky show approaches
stories.summary: Spain is preparing for a rare celestial spectacle as a total solar eclipse crosses the mainland on August 12, bringing brief darkness to parts of the Iberian Peninsula and offering millions across Europe a chance to witness one of astronomy’s most striking events.
stories.post: 📰 NEWS: Spain prepares for rare total solar eclipse as 2026 sky show approaches. Spain is preparing for a rare celestial spectacle as a total solar eclipse crosses the mainland on August 12, bringing brief darkness to parts of the Iberian. Source: Africanews English.
article_sentences: Spain is preparing for a rare celestial spectacle as a total solar eclipse crosses the mainland on August 12, bringing brief darkness to parts of the Iberian Peninsula and offering millions across Europe a chance to witness one of astronomy’s most striking events.
For the first time in more than a century, a total solar eclipse will cross mainland Spain, with the Moon passing directly between the Earth and the Sun.
The eclipse will also be visible across parts of Greenland, Iceland and Portugal, while a partial eclipse will stretch across much of Europe, North America and West Africa.
Totality will last for up to two minutes and 18 seconds along the eclipse path, although the duration will vary depending on location.
Jake Foster, an astronomer at the Royal Observatory Greenwich, says witnessing a total eclipse from the same location is exceptionally rare.
“Well in order to see a total solar eclipse from the very same location more than once, you could be waiting over 200 years for that to happen,” he says.
Partial eclipses are more frequent, but their visibility can still depend heavily on location.
The Moon’s shadow, known as the umbra, will travel roughly 8,260 kilometres across the Earth, beginning near the North Pole and moving south.
Much of its journey will pass over the Atlantic Ocean before reaching Portugal and Spain, where large crowds are expected to gather.
The maximum period of totality will occur off Iceland’s west coast.
By the time the shadow reaches Spain, totality will have shortened to around a minute in some areas before the eclipse moves into the Mediterranean.
Beyond the path of totality, millions more will see the Sun partially covered.
